newsitem.title: USA: Beazer sees Q2 loss after $6 mln writedown.
newsitem.headline: Beazer sees Q2 loss after $6 mln writedown.

text.p: Beazer Homes USA Inc said Monday it expects to record a pretax charge of $6 million, or $0.58 a share, to write down the value of two properties in Nevada, resulting in a net loss during the quarter ended March 31 of between $0.50 and $0.55 per share on a primary basis.
Earnings excluding the charge for the second quarter are expected to be $0.03 to $0.08 per share versus $0.40 in the year-earlier period.
The company said the main reasons for the earnings decrease are reduced home closings and a reduction in gross margins in its Nevada operations.
The two properties involved are Craig Ranch, in North Las Vegas, and Promontory, in Reno/Sparks, Nevada.
The company said the writedown of these two properties results from significant overruns in development costs, the most significant relating to adverse unanticipated ground conditions at Promontory.
Beazer said it expects to report actual results for the quarter on April 30.

The company added that it has reorganized its management structure in Nevada by appointing a new division president for Las Vegas and transferring the management responsibility for the Reno/Sparks property to its management team in Northern California based in Sacramento.

Beazer said it has completed the development of Craig Ranch, and expects to complete the development of Promontory during the current fiscal year and sell out of both of these projects within two years.
